findings.title: Acceptance is recorded but not evidenced: one global version string, written once, never read, with no archived copy of the accepted text and no re-acceptance flow
findings.note: PARTIAL 2026-08-27 (medium-truth). The EVIDENCE half is closed and driven: legal_document_versions archives the published body of all seven documents in both locales, signup writes a tenant.legal_accepted audit row in the same transaction as the Tenant, and GET /t/:slug/legal/consent/evidence returns body + sha256 + who + when + IP per document (consent-evidence.spec.ts + legal-acceptance.spec.ts 8/8; routes confirmed mapped in a real production boot). The retention sweep now explicitly spares tenant.legal_accepted at any period. STILL OPEN: `grep -rn 'legal/consent|reacceptanceRequired' apps/web` returns nothing - reacceptanceRequired is computed, served and tested with no caller, so a library is never prompted to re-accept, and there is no admin view of the record. Both are apps/web, outside this package.

findings.title: The production API image ships the entire dev and web dependency tree — 611 packages, 880 MB, including eslint, vitest, turbo, typescript, Next.js and Prisma Studio
findings.note: VERIFIED 2026-08-27 (medium-truth). DOCKER IS NOT INSTALLED ON THIS MACHINE so no image was built; verified instead against a hardlink replica of the installed workspace, running the exact invocation apps/api/Dockerfile:172 runs. Result: 343 store dirs / 442 MiB removed; eslint@10.9.0, vitest@4.1.11, turbo@2.10.11, next@16.3.2, prettier and supertest all gone from node_modules/.pnpm (grep -c = 0); tsx runs TypeScript, prisma reports 7.9.1, marked imports. Stronger still, the pruned tree BOOTS the real API under NODE_ENV=production and answers GET /metrics 200. RESIDUAL: ~170 MiB of Prisma CLI / studio-core / pglite / mysql2 stays - it is an auto-installed optional peer of a production dependency, so no Dockerfile change can remove it (supply-chain-04). The .github/workflows/verify.yml image-contents job that builds the images has still never run anywhere.

findings.title: Password-reset and email-verification tokens are stored in Redis in plaintext, keyed by the token itself
Mandatory admin-MFA is bypassed by any request path that merely contains `/mfa/` or `/auth/` as a substring
The applicant-PII CSV export is behind AdminRolesGuard but carries no @AdminRoles, so any admin tier can pull it
The go-live doc's webhook step can be completed successfully while nothing is actually wired: the one event a reader would naturally subscribe to is a deliberate no-op
The doc's own pre-flight check — 'check no existing tenant is already over its cap' — cannot be performed in production
The payment-failure banner is hardcoded English on a Greek-first product
NODE_ENV is cast, never validated — a typo silently un-gates the dev-only smoke-test controller, honours RATE_LIMIT_DISABLED, and collapses STORAGE_SIGNING_SECRET into SESSION_SECRET
CONTROL_DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL, PG_SUPERUSER_URL and STORAGE_ROOT are optional() with production-shaped localhost defaults; a missing PG_SUPERUSER_URL boots fully green
PUBLIC_HOST's default disagrees between two blocks of the same compose file and the Caddyfile — an unset value points the browser's API base at the marketing site
Billing flags are not cross-validated and are not echoed at boot: BILLING_ENABLED=true with STRIPE_DRIVER=fake starts silently, and BILLING_ENABLED='enabled' silently means false
/readyz's per-dependency detail is swallowed by the global exception filter, so the readiness probe cannot say what is broken
The web container mounts locales at /srv/libriant/locales but is never told where they are — the mount is inert and the legal/i18n content depends on an unverified in-image path
Postgres is started with LANG=el_GR.UTF-8 on an Alpine (musl) image that has no such locale
The pgbouncer healthcheck proves only that the pooler accepts connections, and nothing depends on it being healthy anyway
findings.note: pgbouncer-probe sidecar runs psql through the pooler; reported by both deploy paths

findings.title: The import pipeline enforces `max_books`/`max_members` from a private in-memory counter outside the advisory-lock domain every other path uses
Member archive and hold placement use different lock domains, so a member can be archived while acquiring a live hold
tenant-relocate lifts the source database's read-only fence before the control-plane cutover and cache bust
Stripe subscription webhooks do multi-statement read-modify-write with no transaction or row lock
`audit_log_retention_days` is priced across five plan tiers but enforced nowhere
Member-number generation runs outside the transaction whose lock its comment claims serialises it
The nightly `storageUsedBytes` recompute that three code comments name as the drift backstop does not exist
Library brand colour is accepted with no contrast check, so a library can make every primary button white-on-yellow at 1.4:1

A NUL byte in any text query parameter produces an HTTP 500, including on the unauthenticated /help/articles endpoint
Deeply nested JSON on unauthenticated endpoints blows the stack inside class-transformer and returns 500
Uploads trust the client's Content-Type entirely; no magic-byte check and no multer fileFilter
The public /apply throttle fails open, and the only bot defence behind it is a honeypot field

The plan catalogue ships three feature flags the product does not have and the site explicitly disclaims — api_access, custom_subdomain, priority_support
A tenant cannot see its own usage against its plan limits in production, so the first signal a library gets when billing turns on is the refusal itself

An aborted dr-drill.sh leaves the shared superuser role crippled (statement_timeout=1s, CONNECTION LIMIT 7)

findings.title: Redis has a 512 MB cgroup ceiling and no maxmemory — an OOM-kill is a full outage
Scheduled BullMQ jobs are registered with no attempts, so they never retry — contradicting the code's own comment
Caddy has no retry budget for its single upstreams — every container recreate is a burst of user-visible 502s
autoInstallPeers pulls the Prisma CLI, Prisma Studio, a MySQL driver and an embedded WASM Postgres into the production dependency closure — and with them the one open CVE
Caddy runs as root, holds the Cloudflare origin private key and the ACME account key, and the compose file states the opposite
findings.note: OPEN. Containment landed and holds: no-new-privileges on all nine services, cap_drop [ALL] on caddy with cap_add REMOVED entirely (the edge now runs with an empty capability set and binds via net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start), an origin-key pre-flight in both deploy paths, and the false "eliminates the only root container" comment deleted. The uid itself is NOT closed: user 1000:0 produced `exec /usr/bin/caddy: operation not permitted` and crash-looped the LIVE edge on 2026-09-02. Three diagnoses were wrong; the last was disproved on the box — getcap empty, binary 0755 root-owned, still refusing to exec as uid 1000. Cause unknown. Reverted to uid 0; docs/RUNBOOK.md 3.7c records the attempt and the one throwaway-container command that would settle it without touching the edge.
